analysis:
The supplied units are base_text lines 898-1873 of docs/threat-model.yaml. They cover T-010 through T-046, including T-041 for the prefix cache, T-033/T-034/T-036 for attestation, and T-044/T-045 for the fan helper. The complete range map shows that the only PR change is at base line 1969 and head lines 1969-1970. That change sits in the T-050 video mitigation and falls outside these units.

The new text widens the documented accepted MIME types for inline video. Previously the mitigation listed data:video/mp4 and data:video/quicktime. It now also lists data:video/x-m4v and data:video/mov, and adds the condition that the payload bytes must be an MP4 or QuickTime file.

The examined units are unchanged and contain no regression. I cannot verify whether provider media-ingestion code actually matches the new MIME allowlist or performs the container byte-sniffing check. This matters for T-050 (TB-003, A-001) and for inline-video attack surface reachable by ADV-002 consumers. The next pass should confirm that the media ingestion source enforces the new allowlist and magic-byte check. It should also confirm that the existing decoded-byte, duration, frame-pixel, video-count and aggregate caps and AVURLAssetReferenceRestrictions.forbidAll still apply to the new aliases. No finding is raised because this is a documentation-only change and the implementation evidence is outside this batch.
